title: Salem MA Home Rebates 2026: Mass Save, Heat Pumps and Solar
desc: Salem, Massachusetts home rebates for 2026: Mass Save heat pump rebates up to $8,500, free assessments, weatherization, solar and EV charger help, with National Grid as the utility.
badge: Up to $8,500 for a whole-home heat pump
lead: Salem is a city of two- and three-family houses: about 38% of its homes sit in buildings of two to four units, and half the households rent. That shapes which Mass Save offers matter most here.
cards_heading: What is open for Salem homes in 2026
cards_intro: Salem's electricity comes from National Grid, so it is covered by Mass Save. Each card below names the program page we read on October 3, 2026. The amounts are statewide, but the right starting point depends on how your building is heated.

cards.title: Whole-home heat pump
cards.note: $2,650 per ton for a whole-home air-source system, up to $8,500, for homes replacing oil, propane or electric resistance heat, or natural gas heat through a gas sponsor. Installed by a Mass Save heat pump installer in 2026.

cards.title: Income-qualified heat pump
cards.note: Enhanced rebates for moderate-income and income-eligible households. This is not the standard amount.

cards.title: Home energy assessment
cards.note: The no-cost assessment unlocks the weatherization offers and tells you what each building needs.

cards.title: Insulation and air sealing
cards.note: 75% is the standard offer. 100% generally applies to income-qualified households or certain buildings with one to four units.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Instant rebate when replacing an electric, oil, propane or gas water heater.

cards.title: Induction cooktop
cards.note: For switching from a gas or propane cooktop. An ENERGY STAR clothes dryer earns $50.

cards.title: Solar (SMART)
cards.note: A flat payment per kWh for systems up to 25 kW; $0.06 for low-income customers. The state tax credit is 15% of cost, up to $1,000.

cards.title: Battery
cards.note: A 5 kW battery enrolled in ConnectedSolutions earns about that over summer events, and the HEAT Loan can finance it at 0%, up to $25,000.

cards.title: Home EV charger wiring
cards.note: National Grid pays up to $700 for a 240-volt circuit, or $1,400 for a charger shared in a two- to four-unit building. Off-peak charging enrollment is required.

sections: The 2020-2024 American Community Survey counts 21,492 housing units in Salem. About 38% are in buildings of two to four units, and only about 24% are detached single-family houses. That matters for three Mass Save rules: the 100% weatherization offer can reach certain one- to four-unit buildings, the shared-charger EV amount is $1,400 for two to four units, and a landlord can be the one who applies. If you own a three-decker and live in one unit, ask the assessor how the whole building will be treated.

About 50% of Salem households rent. The structural rebates, such as heat pumps and insulation, go to whoever owns the building, so a tenant's practical options are the free assessment request (ask the landlord to book it), appliance rebates for anything the tenant buys, and the income-qualified offers if the household qualifies. A tenant who pays the electric bill should still check whether their income fits the enhanced tier.

The ACS estimates 55% of occupied Salem homes heat with utility gas, 25% with electricity and about 17% with fuel oil. The heat pump rebate is written around what you replace. Oil, propane and electric resistance homes qualify through the electric sponsor, and gas homes through the gas sponsor, so a gas-heated three-decker and an oil-heated single-family house in the same street may have different paperwork. Ask the contractor which sponsor applies to your address.

About 76% of Salem's homes were built before 1980, and about 51% before 1940. Homes of that age often have the most to gain from air sealing and insulation, which is why the assessment comes first. The 75% to 100% weatherization offer is usually the largest saving for them, before any heat pump is sized.

Salem is a National Grid town, so it is in Mass Save's electric programs. Several nearby towns, including Peabody, Marblehead and Danvers, are on municipal light plants and use their own rebates instead. If you are comparing offers with a friend in one of those towns, expect the electric side to differ.

Since January 1, 2026 Mass Save has removed heat pumps with a high-warming refrigerant, including R-410A, from its qualified list. Ask which refrigerant is in the unit before you sign, and make sure the installer is on the Mass Save list.
claim_steps: Book the free Mass Save home energy assessment for your building.
Ask the assessor how a two- to four-unit building is treated, and whether your household may qualify for enhanced offers.
Get quotes from a Mass Save heat pump installer and ask which refrigerant the unit uses.
Pick the sponsor route that matches the fuel you are replacing.
Keep invoices and model numbers for the rebate paperwork.
faq: Does Salem get Mass Save rebates?
Yes. Salem is a National Grid electric town, so it is in the Mass Save programs. Some neighbouring towns on municipal light plants are not.
Can the owner of a three-decker get 100% off insulation?
Mass Save says 100% generally applies to income-qualified households or certain buildings with one to four units. The assessor decides which applies to your building.
How much is the heat pump rebate in Salem?
Up to $8,500 for a whole-home system under the standard offer, and no cost or up to $16,000 for income-qualified households.
Can a Salem tenant claim a heat pump rebate?
The owner of the building is usually the one who applies. A tenant can ask the landlord to book an assessment.
Is there a federal tax credit in 2026?
No. The federal home energy credits ended for installs after December 31, 2025.
